learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning and importance of fire,
discuss the possible causes of fire outbreaks in the environment (flammable substances, electrical faults, combustible materials),
share experiences on ways of preventing fire outbreaks in the environment,
discuss firefighting techniques in the work environment, (cooling, smothering, starving, interrupting),
role play fire fighting techniques for extinguishing fire.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is fire safety important?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner acquires active listening and communication skills when following simple instructions to complete tasks while role-playing firefighting techniques in the work environment.
Creativity and Imagination: learner acquires networking skills by undertaking group activities and exchanging new ideas that inspire creative thinking skills during the role-play on firefighting techniques for extinguishing fire.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles and duties when role-playing firefighting techniques.
Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when brainstorming on the possible causes of fire outbreaks in the environment.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety: learner enhances safety awareness when sharing experiences on ways of preventing fire outbreaks in the environment.
sub_strands.links: Integrated Science: learner relates fire safety to fire control measures in Integrated Science.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: lessons: table says 6, summary says 7.

outcomes.text: identify possible causes of fire outbreaks in the environment
explain ways of preventing fire outbreaks in the environment

skills.name: Name the causes of fire outbreaks at home, school and in the community
skills.mastery: The child names causes of fire (a lit candle or match left unattended, faulty or overloaded electrical wiring, an unattended cooking fire or stove, careless disposal of cigarettes, leaking gas, children playing with matches, lightning and dry grass in the hot sun) and does not say fires have only natural causes. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick a cause of fire
say which is a natural and which a human cause
say what a fire needs
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: Grade 7 Pre-Technical Studies taught it first. Proposed, to confirm by a teacher.

skills.name: Pick ways to prevent fire outbreaks
skills.mastery: The child picks ways to prevent fire (keep matches and lighters away from children, store paraffin, petrol and gas safely away from heat, never leave a stove or candle unattended, repair damaged wires, do not overload sockets, keep exits clear and have a fire drill) and does not block exits or store fuel near a stove. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the way to prevent a fire
say what to do with matches and fuel
say what to do with wiring and exits
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: This skill builds on it. Proposed, to confirm by a teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks fires start only from lightning or the sun.

example.question: Which is a common cause of fires in homes?
example.correct_answer: A candle or stove left unattended

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only lightning" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: List the causes of fires near your home.
misconceptions.feedback: Most fires at home start from careless human acts such as an unattended candle or stove.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a safety statement written for Grade 8.

misconceptions.error: Does not know faulty wiring can cause fire.

example.question: Which can cause an electrical fire?

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "A switched-off lamp" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Look for scorch marks on a socket.
misconceptions.feedback: Overloaded sockets and damaged wires get hot and can start a fire.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a safety statement written for Grade 8.

misconceptions.error: Thinks stored paraffin or gas is harmless near heat.

example.question: Why is paraffin kept away from the stove?

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It is only heavy" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask what paraffin is for.
misconceptions.feedback: Fuels burn easily, so they are stored away from heat.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a safety statement written for Grade 8.

misconceptions.error: Leaves matches where children can reach them.

example.question: Where should matches be kept?
example.correct_answer: Out of the reach of children

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "On the kitchen table" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Walk the house and find where matches are kept.
misconceptions.feedback: Matches are kept out of the reach of children.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a safety statement written for Grade 8.

misconceptions.error: Blocks or locks exits.

example.question: Which action helps people escape from a fire?

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Locking the exit door" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Practise a drill.
misconceptions.feedback: Exits must be clear and unlocked in a fire.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a safety statement written for Grade 8.

misconceptions.error: Leaves a stove or candle burning while out of the room.

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Leave it to burn" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Count the times you left a candle.
misconceptions.feedback: Never leave a stove or candle burning unattended.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a safety statement written for Grade 8.

sub_strands.authoring_notes: Outcomes a and b are tested by questions. Outcome c (extinguish fires) is NOT done by learners: the teacher or fire officer demonstrates a blanket, sand or an extinguisher on a small safe fire, and learners only watch and say the steps. skills.name: Say why data matters and name the threats to data on a device
skills.mastery: The child says data (documents, photos, messages, schoolwork) is valuable because it is hard to replace and may be private, and names threats (viruses and other malware, theft or loss of the device, hackers, power failure, accidental deletion, a spoilt storage device), and does not say a virus can only come from the internet. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: say why data is valuable
pick a threat to data
say what a virus does
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: Grade 7 Pre-Technical Studies taught it first. Proposed, to confirm by a teacher.

skills.name: Pick ways to protect data on a device
skills.mastery: The child picks ways to protect data (a strong password that is kept secret, a backup copy on another device, antivirus software kept up to date, locking the screen, not opening unknown links or attachments, keeping the device safe) and does not share a password or keep only one copy. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the way to protect data
say what a good password is
say what a backup is
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: This skill builds on it. Proposed, to confirm by a teacher.

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Share it with a friend" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask who could use your account.
misconceptions.feedback: A password is kept secret.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: Why make a backup?
example.correct_answer: To keep a copy if the device is lost or fails

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It is not needed" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask what happens to the only copy of an essay.
misconceptions.feedback: A backup is a second copy kept on another device.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

sub_strands.authoring_notes: Outcomes a, b and c are tested by questions. Outcome d (secure data on a device) is practical on a school device: set a screen lock, make a backup copy, observed by the teacher; no real password is typed into the system or shared. Outcome e is attitudinal.

skills.name: Name the instruments used in technical drawing and what each does
skills.mastery: The child names the T-square (draws horizontal lines), set squares of 45 and 30/60 degrees (draw upright and slanted lines), the compass (draws circles and arcs), the protractor (measures angles), the ruler (measures lengths), the drawing board, a hard pencil for fine lines and the eraser, and does not mix them up. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the instrument for a task
say what the set square does
say what the compass does
find the false step in a learner's reason

skills.name: Say how a drawing sheet is laid out
skills.mastery: The child says a drawing sheet has a border (a frame drawn a little inside the edges), a title block (name, title, scale, date and sheet number) at the bottom right, a clear working area, and that A4 is 297 by 210 millimetres, and does not put the title block at the top or leave out the border. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the part of the sheet
say where the title block goes
say the size of an A4 sheet
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: This skill builds on it. Proposed, to confirm by a teacher.

skills.name: Name the parts of dimensioning and the types of dimension
skills.mastery: The child names the dimension line (a thin line with arrowheads showing the size), extension lines (thin lines that stretch out from the object), the leader line (points to a note), the figure (written above the dimension line), the symbols for diameter and radius, and says sizes on drawings are normally in millimetres, and does not use the object line as a dimension line. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the line from its job
say where the figure is placed
pick the unit used
find the false step in a learner's reason

skills.name: Read and work out dimensions of given shapes
skills.mastery: The child reads a dimension from the drawing, adds the parts to get the overall length, subtracts to find a missing part, says the diameter is twice the radius, and keeps the unit with the answer. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: read the overall length
work out a missing dimension
work out the diameter from the radius
find the false step in a learner's reason

skills.name: Read a scale and work out real sizes from a drawing
skills.mastery: The child says a scale such as 1:50 means one unit on the drawing stands for 50 of the same unit on the real object, multiplies a drawing length by the scale to get the real length and divides a real length by the scale to get the drawing length, knows 1:1 is full size and 2:1 is an enlargement, and keeps the units. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

find the false step in a learner's reason

Safety and security: learner acquires road safety awareness when brainstorming and presenting information on types of roads and safe vehicles required to market goods and services
sub_strands.links: Social Studies: learner enhances knowledge of trade when discussing marketing of goods and services.

outcomes.text: explain the importance of marketing to a business
analyse the sources of information about the market for its potential customers
explore factors considered when selecting a suitable market for goods and services
select tools to market goods and services
recognise suitable markets for goods and services

skills.name: Say why a business markets, where it learns about the market and how it promotes goods
skills.mastery: The child says marketing helps a business find customers and sell, names sources of market information (asking customers, watching competitors, a survey, the internet, newspapers and radio), names factors in choosing a market (customer demand, price, location, competition, transport) and tools (a poster, radio, social media, samples, a price offer, word of mouth). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: say why marketing matters
pick a source of market information
pick a factor in choosing a market
pick a tool of marketing

prerequisites.reason: This skill builds on it. Proposed, to confirm by a teacher.

misconceptions.error: Says marketing is only selling at the till.

example.question: What does marketing do?
example.wrong_answer: Only takes the money at the till
example.correct_answer: Finds customers and tells them about goods

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only takes the money at the till" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask how customers hear about a new shop.
misconceptions.feedback: Marketing helps a business find customers and sell.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Guessing" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask what a shopkeeper asks customers.
misconceptions.feedback: A survey, asking customers and watching competitors give market information.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Names a factor that does not matter in choosing a market.

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The colour of the shop" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask where people buy shoes.
misconceptions.feedback: Demand, price, location, competition and transport matter in choosing a market.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Names something that is not a marketing tool.

example.question: Which is a marketing tool?

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.

misconceptions.help: List ways you heard about a product.
misconceptions.feedback: Posters, radio, social media, samples and offers are marketing tools.

learning_experiences: discuss and present the meaning of channels of distribution and role of intermediaries in distribution of goods and services,
search from available resources the role of intermediaries in distribution of goods and services to the consumer,
search and watch video clips on channels for distributing different goods and services,
prepare a chart on channels for distribution of different goods and services,
read and discuss stories on different distribution channels for goods and services,
debate on ethical and unethical practices on distribution of goods and services.
key_inquiry_questions: How is the distribution of goods and services carried out in day-to-day life?
Which ethical issues influence distribution of goods and services?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: learner acquires the skills of interacting with digital devices when watching and listening to video clips on channels for distributing goods and services.
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner acquires interpretation and inference skills when debating on ethical issues in distribution of goods and services.
sub_strands.values:
Respect: learner develops regard for self and others when discussing the meaning of channels of distribution and role of intermediaries in the distribution of goods and services.
Peace: learner displays tolerance and respect for others when debating on ethical issues on distribution of goods and services.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Cohesion: learner improves on their interpersonal relationships when debating on ethical issues on distribution of goods and services.
sub_strands.links: Social Studies: learner enhances knowledge on trade when learning about distribution of goods and services.

outcomes.text: explain the role of intermediaries in the distribution of goods and services
illustrate the channels for distributing different goods and services in business
analyse ethics in distribution of goods and services
value the need for distribution of goods and services in the community

skills.name: Say what intermediaries do, the channels of distribution and ethics in distribution
skills.mastery: The child names intermediaries (wholesalers who sell in bulk to retailers, retailers who sell to buyers, agents who bring buyers and sellers together), puts channels in order (producer to consumer; producer to retailer to consumer; producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer), and picks ethical practices (honest weights and measures, fair prices, safe delivery, not hoarding) over unethical ones. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the intermediary
put the channel in order
pick the ethical practice
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: This skill builds on it. Proposed, to confirm by a teacher.

misconceptions.error: Says intermediaries only raise the price and have no use.

example.question: What does a wholesaler do?
example.correct_answer: Buys in bulk and sells to retailers

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Nothing useful" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Follow a bag of maize from farm to shop.
misconceptions.feedback: Intermediaries bring goods from producers to buyers.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Puts the channel in the wrong order.

example.question: Which is the longest channel?
example.correct_answer: Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Producer to consumer" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Draw the chain with arrows.
misconceptions.feedback: The longest channel has a wholesaler and a retailer between producer and consumer.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks hoarding or cheating on weights is fine.

example.question: Which is ethical in distribution?
example.wrong_answer: Hiding goods to raise the price
example.correct_answer: Giving honest weights and fair prices

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up two ideas that sound alike or are taught close together.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Hiding goods to raise the price" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
misconceptions.help: Ask what a customer wants from a trader.
misconceptions.feedback: Honest weights, fair prices and safe delivery are ethical. Hoarding and cheating are not.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

sub_strands.authoring_notes: Outcomes a, b and c are tested by questions. Outcome d is attitudinal.

indicators.indicator: Ability to extinguish fires in the environment using appropriate methods. Ability to describe ways of protecting data in an electronic device.

levels.EE: Extinguishes fires in the environment using four appropriate methods. Comprehensively describes ways of protecting data in an electronic device.
levels.ME: Extinguishes fires in the environment using three appropriate methods. Describes ways of protecting data in an electronic device.
levels.AE: Extinguishes fires in the environment using two appropriate methods. Describes some of the ways of protecting data in an electronic device.
levels.BE: Extinguishes fires in the environment using only one appropriate method. Describes a few ways of protecting data in an electronic device.
